mainTopic: Eating the מנחה as a מצוה (and חלוט as מצה), then who inherits the dead brother's estate after חליצה or יבום
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: the מנחה was permitted, then forbidden, then permitted again, and the פסוק 'מצות תאכל במקום קדוש' teaches that eating it is a מצוה. According to רבא, this means the כהן who prepares it should eat it himself rather than give it to another כהן. According to רב יצחק בר אבדימי (following אבא שאול), the גמרא looks for two ways of eating it. It rejects overeating and חמץ, and settles on baked מצה versus חלוט. The גמרא then explains that חלוט counts as מצה. It is invalid for a מנחה only because the פסוק repeats the requirement, but once baked in an oven it works for מצה on פסח. A new משנה teaches that a brother who does חליצה shares the estate equally with his brothers. A brother who does יבום takes the whole estate, and רבי יהודה says a living father takes it either way. The גמרא explains each clause and gives רבי יהודה's source, comparing the יבם to a בכור. It ends with רבי ינאי and רב נחמן ruling that the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה. The amud closes with the start of a new משנה: after חליצה, each side is forbidden to the other's relatives.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: the permitted-forbidden-permitted pattern
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its point. The item was first permitted, then became forbidden, then became permitted again. One might think it simply goes back to its old status, so the פסוק teaches it is a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first it was permitted to him like any other food. Then it became forbidden, and then it became permitted again. You might think it goes back to its first kind of permission. So the פסוק says: 'It shall be eaten as מצות in a holy place.' This means it is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא quoted just before this, which uses the פסוק about the מנחה to show that eating it is a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning works in three stages: permitted, then forbidden once it became holy, then permitted again. Without a פסוק we might think the new permission is just like the old one, a plain option. The word 'מצוה' tells us the new permission comes with an obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: Among permitted things; allowed like ordinary food
Therefore the פסוק says (to teach otherwise)

phrases.english: For at first it was, for him,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the flour of the מנחה, before it was made holy.

phrases.english: among the permitted things.
It became forbidden, and then became permitted again.
phrases.notes: It became forbidden when it was made holy, and permitted again once the handful was offered on the מזבח.

phrases.english: One might think it goes back to its original permitted status —
therefore the verse says:
"It shall be eaten as unleavened bread in a holy place" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:9

phrases.english: it is a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted earlier in the סוגיא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the מנחה is permitted again, the פסוק 'מצות תאכל במקום קדוש' teaches that eating it is a מצוה.

steps.title: Reading the מנחה clause according to רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins with 'בשלמא לרבא': according to רבא, who says the ברייתא follows the רבנן, the clause means the כהן might have thought he could eat it or not, and the פסוק says it is a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רבא, who said this ברייתא follows the רבנן. Here the ברייתא means this: 'It shall be eaten as מצות in a holy place' teaches that it is a מצוה. At first it was permitted to him: if he wanted he ate it, and if he wanted he did not. It became forbidden, then permitted again. You might think it goes back to its first permission, so that if he wants he eats it and if he wants he doesn't.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with 'בשלמא' ('this works well for') and shows how רבא would explain the מנחה clause. This sets up a comparison, since it hints that the other view will have a harder time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, 'מצוה' teaches an obligation where we might have thought there was only a choice. So the גמרא fills in the 'you might think' part: the כהן may eat it or not, as he likes. This first reading is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (for this view); often sets up a challenge to the other view
If he wants, he eats it

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final reading. It is a first try that gets rejected in the very next step.

phrases.english: This works well for Rava, who said:
Whose view is this? It is the Rabbis' —
here, this is what it is saying:
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the first clause of the ברייתא, the one about the מנחה.

phrases.english: "It shall be eaten as unleavened bread in a holy place" — it is a מצוה.
For at first it was among the permitted things for him:
if he wanted, he ate it; if he wanted, he did not eat it.
(It became forbidden, then became permitted again;
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets; the point reads the same either way.

phrases.english: one might think it goes back to its original permitted status),
so if he wants he eats it, and if he wants he does not eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרָבָא דְּאָמַר הָא מַנִּי רַבָּנַן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ברייתא from step 1 according to רבא's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does רבא's view (the ברייתא follows the רבנן) explain the 'you might think' and the 'מצוה' in the מנחה clause?

steps.title: A כהן cannot simply choose not to eat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: how could the כהן ever choose not to eat it? A פסוק teaches that the כהנים' eating is what brings כפרה to the owners.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If he wants, he doesn't eat it'?! But it is written: 'And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made.' This teaches that the כהנים eat and the owners gain atonement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reading from step 2 because it allows the כהן to skip eating altogether.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows that the כהנים' eating is part of the owners' כפרה. So eating the קרבן was never optional, and no one would have thought it was. The 'you might think' of step 2 can't be right.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written! (a challenge from a פסוק)
The owners who brought the קרבן

phrases.english: If he wants, he doesn't eat it?!
But it is written:
"And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made,"
phrases.notes: שמות 29:33

phrases.english: which teaches that the priests eat
and the owners gain atonement!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading offered in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea in step 2 that the כהן may choose not to eat the מנחה at all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק teaches that the כהנים' eating brings כפרה to the owners, so eating could never have been optional.

steps.title: The real doubt: this כהן or another כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the clause. The choice was never whether to eat. It was whether he eats it or another כהן eats it. The פסוק teaches it is a מצוה for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means: if he wants, he eats it, and if he wants, another כהן eats it. So the פסוק says: 'It shall be eaten as מצות in a holy place.' It is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes its reading of רבא's explanation. The 'choice' was who eats the מנחה, not whether it gets eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחה must be eaten by some כהן either way, so the קשיא is answered. What we might have thought optional is which כהן eats it. 'מצוה' teaches that this כהן himself should eat it. This keeps רבא's idea that the ברייתא teaches a מצוה where we might have thought there was only a choice.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the מנחה clause does not teach that eating is required, since that is already known. It teaches that it is a מצוה for this particular כהן to eat it himself, not hand it to another כהן.

phrases.english: Rather: if he wants, he eats it,
and if he wants, another priest eats it;
therefore the verse says: "It shall be eaten as unleavened bread in a holy place" —
it is a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: רָצָה הוּא אוֹכְלָהּ, רָצָה כֹּהֵן אַחֵר אוֹכְלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3 by changing what the 'you might think' was about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא: the option is about who eats, not whether it is eaten.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the כהן could hand the מנחה to any other כהן to eat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that it is a מצוה for this כהן himself to eat it, and this fits רבא's view that the ברייתא follows the רבנן.

steps.title: What two ways of eating fit רב יצחק בר אבדימי's reading?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to רב יצחק בר אבדימי, who says the ברייתא follows אבא שאול, and asks: in this clause about the מנחה, what two ways of eating could there be?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב יצחק בר אבדימי, who said the ברייתא is אבא שאול, what two ways are there here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves רבא, whose reading worked, and challenges the other reading. For רב יצחק בר אבדימי, the ברייתא must be choosing between two ways of eating, and the גמרא asks what those two ways are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אבא שאול, the ברייתא is about doing the act the right way rather than a wrong way. So the clause 'one might think he can eat it either way' needs two real ways of eating, one proper and one not. With the מנחה it is not obvious what the second way could be.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who stresses that a מצוה must be done in the proper way and for the right reason
Here, meaning in this clause of the ברייתא

phrases.english: But according to Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi,
who said it is the view of Abba Shaul,
here, what two ways are there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with the בשלמא לרבא line: that reading worked, but this one seems hard.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יצחק בר אבדימי's claim that the ברייתא follows אבא שאול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His reading needs two possible ways of eating the מנחה, and none is clear.

steps.title: Suggestion: eating with appetite vs. overeating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the two ways might be eating the מנחה with appetite or eating it while already full.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: if he wants, he eats it with appetite; if he wants, he eats it as overeating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer. Maybe the two ways are eating it normally, when hungry, or forcing it down when already stuffed. The next step will test this idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This would give אבא שאול a proper way (eating with appetite) and an improper way (overeating). The פסוק would then teach that only the proper way is the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say; this opens a suggested answer that is usually rejected
With appetite, eating normally while hungry
Overeating, eating when already completely full

phrases.english: And if you would say: if he wishes, he eats it with appetite,
if he wishes, he eats it as excessive eating,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first candidate for the 'two ways' asked about in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the two options as two manners of eating
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No second way of eating the מנחה seems to exist.
steps.terutzMaskana: Appetite versus overeating might be the two ways (tested next).

steps.title: Overeating is not counted as eating
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected: ריש לקיש rules that someone who overeats on יום הכיפורים is exempt, which shows overeating is not halachic eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is overeating called eating? Didn't ריש לקיש say that one who overeats on יום הכיפורים is exempt from 'shall not be afflicted'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggestion from step 6. Overeating does not count as eating at all, so it cannot be a second 'way of eating' the מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש rules that someone who forces food down when already full on יום הכיפורים is not punished. This shows that הלכה does not treat overeating as eating. So 'eating it as overeating' is not really a way of eating it, and step 6 fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it called? Does it count as?
An אמורא, רבי שמעון בן לקיש
The Day of Atonement, when eating is forbidden
'Shall not be afflicted', the פסוק that brings כרת for eating on יום הכיפורים

steps.confusionAlert: Overeating is still not a good thing to do. ריש לקיש only means it does not count as halachic 'eating', so it cannot serve as one of the two ways of eating the מנחה.

phrases.english: Is excessive eating called eating?
But didn't Reish Lakish say:
one who eats excessively on Yom Kippur
is exempt from 'shall not be afflicted'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:29

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects 'appetite vs. overeating' as the two ways
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Overeating is not halachic eating, so it cannot be a second way of eating.

steps.title: Second suggestion: eating it as מצה or as חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests instead that the two ways are about how the מנחה was prepared: as מצה or as חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: if he wants, he eats it as מצה; if he wants, he eats it as חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new pair of options. Instead of how much he eats, maybe the choice is about the food itself: unleavened or leavened. The next step will test this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This moves the 'two ways' from the act of eating to the form of the food. The פסוק would then teach that the proper way is eating it as מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: A flour offering; the כהנים eat what is left after part is burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rather: if he wishes, he eats it as matzah,
if he wishes, he eats it as chametz.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: רָצָה — מַצָּה אוֹכְלָהּ, רָצָה — חָמֵץ אוֹכְלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected suggestion of steps 6-7 with a new pair of options.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the two options as two forms of the food
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ways were about how he eats (appetite vs. overeating).
steps.terutzMaskana: The two ways might be eating it as מצה or as חמץ (tested next).

steps.title: The כהנים' portion may never be חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the פסוק says 'their portion shall not be baked חמץ', and ריש לקיש explains this forbids even the כהנים' portion from being חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written 'their portion shall not be baked חמץ', and ריש לקיש said: even their portion may not be baked חמץ!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the מצה/חמץ suggestion. The Torah already forbids baking the כהנים' share as חמץ, so the ברייתא could not have imagined he might eat it as חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש reads 'חלקם' to include the כהנים' share. If baking it as חמץ is already an outright prohibition, nobody would have thought it was an acceptable option, so this cannot be the second 'way'.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? It brings a פסוק as an objection
Their portion, the part of the מנחה that the כהנים eat

phrases.english: But isn't it written: 'Their portion shall not be baked leavened',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:10

phrases.english: and Reish Lakish said:
even their portion shall not be baked leavened!
phrases.notes: 'Even' means not only the part burned on the מזבח, but also the share the כהנים eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the two ways are מצה vs. חמץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Baking the כהנים' portion as חמץ is already forbidden by a פסוק, so it could never have seemed like a permitted option.

steps.title: Final answer: eating it as מצה or as חלוט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the two ways are eating the מנחה as baked מצה or as חלוט, dough scalded in boiling water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: if he wants, he eats it as מצה; if he wants, he eats it as חלוט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final pair of options that works for רב יצחק בר אבדימי. One might have thought he could eat it either as מצה or as scalded dough, so the פסוק teaches that the מצוה is to eat it as מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלוט is not חמץ, so no פסוק forbids it outright, and it is real eating, unlike overeating. That makes it a genuine second way of eating that someone might have thought was acceptable. With this, the clause fits אבא שאול's idea of doing the מצוה in its proper way.

keyTerms.meaning: Dough scalded or boiled in hot water instead of baked
If he wishes... if he wishes; the pattern for two possible options

steps.whatToRemember: For רב יצחק בר אבדימי (following אבא שאול), the ברייתא's 'either way' means: one might think the מנחה could be eaten as מצה or as חלוט, and the פסוק teaches that the מצוה is מצה. Two attempts fail first: overeating does not count as eating, and חמץ is already forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the סוגיא's goal: the ברייתא clause can be explained according to both רבא and רב יצחק בר אבדימי.

phrases.english: Rather: if he wishes, he eats it as matzah,
if he wishes, he eats it as boiled dough.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: רָצָה — מַצָּה אוֹכְלָהּ, רָצָה — חָלוּט אוֹכְלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected מצה/חמץ suggestion with מצה/חלוט, answering step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the second option as a permitted but improper method of preparation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second option was חמץ, which is already forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second option is חלוט; the פסוק teaches the מצוה is to eat it as מצה.

steps.title: Is scalded dough מצה or not?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that חלוט could even be a question: either it is מצה and allowed, or it is not מצה and clearly forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the status of this scalded dough? If it counts as מצה, then it is מצה and should be allowed. If it does not count as מצה, then רחמנא already said the מנחה must be 'מצות,' so it is obviously forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer from step 10, that the two ways of eating the מנחה are baked מצה or חלוט. It asks how חלוט could be a real question at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There seem to be only two options. If חלוט is מצה, there is no reason to forbid it. If it is not מצה, the פסוק already forbids it. Either way there is nothing to discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What is its status?
The Merciful One (ה׳, as the Torah's author)

phrases.english: This scalded dough, what is its status?

phrases.aramaic: אִי מַצָּה הִיא — הָא מַצָּה הִיא,
phrases.english: If it is מצה, then it is מצה (and should be allowed),
and if it is not מצה,
the Merciful One said 'מצות'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:12. The מנחה must be eaten as מצה, so non-מצה would plainly be forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 10 that חלוט is one of the two ways of eating the מנחה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that eating the מנחה as חלוט is a real open question.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Either option settles the matter. If it is מצה, it is allowed. If it is not, the פסוק forbids it. So there is nothing to ask.

steps.title: It is מצה, but the פסוק's repetition invalidates it
steps.stepSummary: חלוט really is מצה, but the פסוק repeated the requirement of מצה to demand baked מצה, which disqualifies חלוט for the מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, I can tell you it is מצה. But that is exactly why the פסוק repeated the requirement: to make it a must, which rules out חלוט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that חלוט counts as מצה. Even so, the פסוק adds an extra requirement that disqualifies it for the מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קשיא assumed that 'מצה' is the only test. The answer is that the extra wording in the פסוק makes a specific form required. So a מנחה eaten as חלוט is disqualified even though חלוט is מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (I stick with my position)
To make it an absolute requirement (without it, it is invalid)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think חלוט stops being מצה. It is still מצה. It is only disqualified for the מנחה because of the extra requirement in the פסוק.

phrases.english: No, really I can tell you
it is מצה,
and for this reason the verse repeated it
to make it a must.
phrases.notes: The repeated word makes baked מצה required, so a מנחה eaten as חלוט doesn't count.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ מַצָּה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a third option: it is מצה, yet a repeated פסוק disqualifies it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If חלוט is מצה, it must be allowed for the מנחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: חלוט is מצה, but the repeated פסוק requires a specific form, so it is invalid for the מנחה.

steps.title: Then where does 'חלוט is מצה' matter?
steps.stepSummary: If חלוט is disqualified for the מנחה, the גמרא asks what practical law follows from calling it מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this statement we made, that חלוט is מצה, what law does it matter for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. If חלוט can't be used for the מנחה, what difference does it make that it counts as מצה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the פסוק disqualified חלוט for the מנחה, calling it 'מצה' seems to have no effect anywhere. The גמרא wants a case where that label actually matters.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: But (the statement) that scalded dough is מצה
which we said,
for what law does it matter?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא חָלוּט מַצָּה הִיא דְּקָאָמְרִינַן לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 12's answer, which left the label 'מצה' with no apparent effect.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical law for which חלוט counts as מצה.

steps.title: Scalded-then-baked dough works for מצה on פסח
steps.stepSummary: חלוט that was afterward baked in an oven counts as 'לחם עוני,' so a person fulfills the מצוה of eating מצה on פסח with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches that a person fulfills his obligation of מצה on פסח with it. Even though he scalded it at first, he then baked it in an oven, so we call it 'לחם עוני' (bread of affliction), and a person fulfills his obligation with it on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the label matters for פסח. Dough that was scalded and later baked in an oven is good מצה for the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scalding at the start does not stop it from being מצה. Once it is baked in an oven, it fits the פסוק's description 'לחם עוני.' So the מנחה needs a stricter form because of its own פסוק, while for פסח this is enough.
steps.whatToRemember: חלוט is מצה. It is invalid for a מנחה because the פסוק repeats the requirement. But if it was later baked in an oven, it is fine for the מצוה of eating מצה on פסח.

phrases.english: To teach that a person fulfills with it
his obligation on פסח,
even though he scalded it at first,
since he then went back and baked it in an oven,
we call it 'bread of affliction,'
phrases.notes: דברים 16:3

phrases.english: and a person fulfills with it
his obligation on פסח.

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹמַר שֶׁאָדָם יוֹצֵא בָּהּ יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בְּפֶסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It matters for eating מצה on פסח: חלוט that was later baked in an oven counts as 'לחם עוני.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the long סוגיא about the כהנים eating a מנחה. It also gives a practical rule for which מצה is valid on פסח.

steps.title: משנה: Inheritance after חליצה versus יבום
steps.stepSummary: A brother who does חליצה shares the dead brother's estate equally with the other brothers, or the father takes it if he is alive. A brother who does יבום takes the estate himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who does חליצה with his יבמה is like any one of the brothers for the inheritance. If the father is alive, the property goes to the father. One who marries his יבמה through יבום acquires his brother's property.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches who inherits the dead brother's property, depending on whether the surviving brother did חליצה or יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חליצה gives the brother no special share. Normal inheritance rules apply, so the brothers split the estate, or the living father takes all of it. יבום gives the brother who marries the widow the whole estate. Here the first opinion says nothing about a father, so the יבם takes the estate even if the father is alive. That is the point רבי יהודה disputes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: His brother's widow, who needs יבום or חליצה

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who does חליצה with his yevama
is like one of the brothers
for the inheritance.
And if there is a father,
phrases.notes: The dead man's father, still alive. A father inherits before the brothers do.

phrases.english: the property goes to the father.
One who marries his yevama
acquires his brother's property.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַחוֹלֵץ לִיבִמְתּוֹ הֲרֵי הוּא כְּאֶחָד מִן הָאַחִין לַנַּחֲלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It does not continue the מנחה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חליצה gives no extra share: the brothers split the estate, or the father takes it. יבום gives the יבם his brother's property.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: A living father always inherits
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that whether the brother did חליצה or יבום, if the father is alive the property goes to the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Either way, whether he did חליצה or יבום, if there is a father, the property goes to the father.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה, for the case of יבום when the father is still alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said a living father takes the estate only after חליצה. רבי יהודה says the father takes it even after יבום. So in his view, יבום does not push aside the father's right to inherit.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees: after חליצה, normal inheritance applies. The argument is about יבום when the father is alive. The first opinion gives the estate to the יבם. רבי יהודה gives it to the father.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
either way,
phrases.notes: Whether the brother did חליצה or יבום.

phrases.english: if there is a father,
the property goes to the father.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion in step 15 about יבום when the father is alive.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a living father, the property goes to the father, after either חליצה or יבום.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needed to teach that the brother who does חליצה inherits like the other brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking why the משנה needed to say that the brother who does חליצה is like one of the brothers. This question sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the brother who does יבום takes the whole estate. So it seems obvious that a brother who did חליצה gets no special share. The גמרא wants to know what new idea the משנה is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. The גמרא is asking why something needed to be said at all.
The discussion that explains the משנה.

phrases.english: גמרא: It is obvious!
phrases.notes: This is about the first line of the משנה from step 15: the brother who does חליצה shares equally with the other brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's analysis of the משנה's first clause, given in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new idea does the clause 'he is like one of the brothers' teach?

steps.title: We might have thought חליצה replaces יבום
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought that חליצה stands in place of יבום, so the brother who does חליצה would take the whole estate. The משנה teaches that he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that חליצה takes the place of יבום, so he should take all the property. The משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer. Without the משנה, we might have given the brother who does חליצה the whole estate, the same as the brother who does יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חליצה is the other way of dealing with the יבמה. So we might have treated it like יבום and given that brother everything. The משנה tells us he only gets an equal share.

keyTerms.meaning: It could have entered your mind to say. This introduces a mistaken idea.
חליצה stands in the place of יבום.
It teaches us. This tells us what the משנה adds.

phrases.english: It could enter your mind to say
that חליצה stands in the place of יבום,
and he should take all the property,
so it teaches us that this is not so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה rules out the idea that חליצה replaces יבום and earns the whole estate.

steps.title: The wording does not fit that answer
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה meant to limit him, it should have said 'he is only like one of the brothers,' not 'he is like one of the brothers.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say 'he is like one of the brothers'? It should have said 'he is only like one of the brothers'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first answer by looking closely at the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the point were to take something away from him, the משנה would say 'only.' The wording 'he is like one of the brothers' sounds like it is protecting his share. So the first answer does not match the words of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. This introduces a challenge to what was just said.
He is only. This language limits something.

steps.confusionAlert: Look carefully at the difference between 'he is like one of the brothers' and 'he is ONLY like one of the brothers.' The first wording protects his share, while the second takes something away. That one word is what this whole challenge depends on.

phrases.english: If so,
why does it say 'he is like one of the brothers'?
'He is only like one of the brothers'
is what it should have said!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה rules out the brother taking everything.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Limiting language would use 'only.' The actual wording sounds like it protects his share.

steps.title: We might have thought to penalize him
steps.stepSummary: Since he ruined the chance of יבום, we might have thought he should be penalized and lose his share. The משנה teaches that he keeps a normal share.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you might have thought: since he made her lose the chance of יבום, we should penalize him. The משנה teaches us that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer that fits the wording. The משנה is protecting his share, not cutting it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the worry runs the other way. Maybe the brother who did חליצה should lose his share, because he ended the possibility of יבום. The משנה says no: he still inherits like every other brother.

keyTerms.meaning: Since he caused her to lose the chance of יבום.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's point is that the brother who does חליצה is not punished. He keeps his full, equal share of the estate.

phrases.english: Rather, it could enter your mind to say:
since he made her lose the chance of יבום,
let us penalize him. So it teaches us that we do not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer from step 18 with one that fits the wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New understanding of what the משנה is coming to rule out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He should be penalized and lose his share because he ended the chance of יבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is not penalized. He inherits equally like any other brother.

steps.title: Why the father takes the estate
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if the father is alive, he takes the estate. The source is the rule that a father comes before all of his descendants.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If there is a father there': as the Master said, a father comes before all who came out of his thigh (his descendants).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה and gives its source in the laws of inheritance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brothers are all the father's descendants. The rule is that a father comes first in inheriting from his son, before anyone descended from that father. So while the father is alive, the brothers get nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: As the Master said. This introduces a known teaching.
Those who came out of his thigh, meaning his descendants.

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the basic order of inheritance. It is also the background for רבי יהודה's view in step 16.

phrases.english: 'If there is a father there.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה's words from step 15.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
A father comes before all who came out of his thigh.
phrases.notes: He means the father's own descendants, such as the dead man's brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's ruling that the father takes the estate.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The inheritance rule: אב קודם לכל יוצאי ירכו.

steps.title: Why does the brother who marries the widow inherit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and asks for the source of the rule that the יבם inherits his brother's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said that one who marries his brother's widow gets the dead brother's property. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks for its reason. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 17-20 dealt with the brother who does חליצה. Now the גמרא turns to the brother who does יבום. The משנה gave him the whole estate, and the גמרא wants to know where that comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: His brother's widow, who waits for יבום

phrases.english: One who marries his yevama, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which says he gets his dead brother's property.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the חליצה discussion and the father rule to the next clause of the משנה, about the brother who does יבום.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that the יבם inherits his dead brother's estate.

steps.title: He rises up in his brother's name
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the יבם 'rises up in his brother's name.' Since he has taken his brother's place, he also takes his brother's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah says 'he shall rise up in the name of his brother,' and this man has risen up in his place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק: the יבם steps into his dead brother's place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stepping into the brother's place covers more than the marriage. Because he truly takes over for his brother, he also takes over his brother's estate.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall rise up in his brother's name
And he has risen up (taken his place)

phrases.english: "He shall rise up in the name of his brother"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:6

phrases.english: the Merciful One said,
and he has risen up in his place.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָקוּם עַל שֵׁם אָחִיו אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'יקום על שם אחיו' makes the יבם his brother's successor, so he inherits his estate.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the יבם, unlike the brother who does חליצה, gets the whole estate.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: עולא and רבי יצחק נפחא both rule like רבי יהודה, who says that if the father is alive, the estate goes to the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה brought רבי יהודה's opinion. עולא said the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, and רבי יצחק נפחא said the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's view from the משנה, and two אמוראים rule that the הלכה follows him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה said that whether the brother did יבום or חליצה, a living father takes the estate. Two אמוראים rule this way, but later steps bring רבי ינאי and רב נחמן, who rule that the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יצחק the smith, an אמורא

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: either way, if the father is alive, the property goes to him.

phrases.english: Ulla said: The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda.
And likewise Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה, רבי יהודה's view, and gives a ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to עולא and רבי יצחק נפחא, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה: if the father is alive, the estate goes to the father, not to the יבם.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is one side of a dispute about the final הלכה. Later on this amud, רבי ינאי (step 31) and the תנא approved by רב נחמן (steps 32-35) rule that the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The יבם is compared to a בכור
steps.stepSummary: The reason for רבי יהודה: the פסוק calls the יבם 'the בכור.' A בכור gets nothing while his father is alive, so the יבם also gets nothing while the father is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא (some say רבי יצחק נפחא) said: What is רבי יהודה's reason? The פסוק says 'and it shall be the firstborn that she bears.' This means the יבם is like a firstborn. A firstborn has nothing while his father is alive, so this יבם also has nothing while the father is alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source from the פסוק for רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בכור' in the פסוק is read as referring to the יבם himself. That links him to a firstborn son. A firstborn's rights only start after his father dies, so the יבם's rights to the estate also wait until the father dies.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (it was someone else who said it)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר עוּלָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא:
phrases.english: And Ulla said, and some say it was Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?
As it is written: "And it shall be that the firstborn that she bears"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:6. The 'firstborn' here is being read as the יבם himself.

phrases.aramaic: כִּבְכוֹר, מָה בְּכוֹר אֵין לוֹ בְּחַיֵּי הָאָב —
phrases.english: He is like a firstborn: just as a firstborn has nothing during the father's lifetime,

phrases.aramaic: אַף הַאי נָמֵי אֵין לוֹ בְּחַיֵּי הָאָב.
phrases.english: so too this one also has nothing during the father's lifetime.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the ruling in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's rule that a living father takes the estate instead of the יבם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'והיה הבכור אשר תלד,' which compares the יבם to a בכור, who has no rights while his father is alive.

steps.title: Then he should get a double portion too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the comparison: if the יבם is like a בכור, then just as a בכור gets a double portion after the father dies, the יבם should get a double portion too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, then just as a firstborn takes a double portion after the father dies, this one should also take a double portion after the father dies!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the comparison from step 25 by pushing it one step further.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we compare the יבם to a בכור for one rule (nothing during the father's life), why not for the other rule (a double portion after his death)? That would mean his own share plus his dead brother's share. The halacha is not like that, so the comparison seems to prove too much.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the יבם really gets a double portion. The גמרא is only pointing out a problem with the comparison, and the next step answers it.

phrases.aramaic: אִי: מָה בְּכוֹר נוֹטֵל פִּי שְׁנַיִם
phrases.english: If so: just as a firstborn takes a double portion
after the father's death,
so too this one should take a double portion
after the father's death!
phrases.notes: He means: his own share plus the share his dead brother would have gotten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי: מָה בְּכוֹר נוֹטֵל פִּי שְׁנַיִם לְאַחַר מִיתַת הָאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison to a בכור made in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between the יבם and a בכור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison holds for having nothing during the father's life, it should also hold for the double portion after his death. Since the יבם does not get a double portion, the comparison seems flawed.

steps.title: The יבם replaces his brother, not his father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 26. The יבם does not get a double portion, because the פסוק says he rises up in his brother's name, not in his father's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the פסוק say "he shall rise up in the name of his father"? It says "he shall rise up in the name of his brother," and not "in the name of his father."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of why the יבם does not get a double portion like a real בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור's double portion comes from the father's estate. The פסוק only puts the יבם in his brother's place, so he gets his brother's share and nothing extra from the father. The comparison to a בכור teaches only that he gets nothing while the father is alive. It does not give him the double portion.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written...? A way of saying the פסוק does not actually say this
He shall rise up in the name of his brother (דברים 25:6)
The double portion a בכור gets from his father's estate

phrases.english: Is it written, "He shall rise up in the name of his father"?
It is written, "He shall rise up in the name of his brother,"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:6

phrases.english: and not "in the name of his father."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the comparison by reading the פסוק closely
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the יבם is like a בכור in every way, he should get a double portion of the father's estate
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק makes him his brother's replacement only, so he gets no extra share from the father's estate

steps.title: Maybe יבום applies only when the יבם inherits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that if inheritance depends on whether the father is alive, maybe the מצוה of יבום depends on it too. Then יבום would apply only when there is no living father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: where there is no father, so the יבם takes the inheritance, the מצוה of יבום should apply. Where there is a father, so he does not take the inheritance, the מצוה of יבום should not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new difficulty with רבי יהודה's view. If the inheritance in the יבום פסוקים depends on the father not being alive, maybe the whole מצוה of יבום depends on that as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inheritance and יבום appear together in the same פסוקים. If רבי יהודה limits the inheritance to cases with no living father, the same limit might seem to apply to the מצוה itself. That would be a strange result, because then there would be no יבום whenever the father is still alive.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / perhaps we should say. It introduces a suggestion
The מצוה for a brother to marry his dead brother's childless widow

phrases.english: Say: where there is no father,
so that he takes the inheritance,
the מצוה of levirate marriage should apply;
where there is a father,
so that he does not take the inheritance,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording. Without it, the line would not make sense.

phrases.english: the מצוה of levirate marriage should not apply.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא אָב דְּלִשְׁקוֹל נַחֲלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new difficulty that comes out of רבי יהודה's view
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's rule that the יבם does not inherit while the father is alive
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the inheritance part of the פסוקים depends on the father being gone, then the יבום part of the same פסוקים should depend on it too. That would cancel יבום whenever the father is alive.

steps.title: יבום does not depend on inheritance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. The Torah never made יבום depend on inheritance. יבום always happens, and the inheritance follows only if it is available.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did the Torah make יבום depend on inheritance? They perform יבום in every case. If there is an inheritance, he takes it. If not, he does not take it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the idea from step 28. יבום is a מצוה on its own, and the inheritance is a separate matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of יבום stands by itself. Inheritance is just an extra result that comes along when it can. When the father is alive there is simply no inheritance for the יבם, but the יבום still takes place.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah / ה׳

steps.whatToRemember: יבום always applies. The inheritance is a separate result that the יבם receives only when there is an estate he is entitled to.

phrases.english: Did the Merciful One make levirate marriage dependent on inheritance?
They definitely perform levirate marriage,
and if there is an inheritance, he takes it,
and if not, he does not take it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 28
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole idea that the מצוה of יבום depends on whether the יבם inherits
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly ties the מצוה to the inheritance, when the Torah treats them as separate

steps.title: רבי חנינא rules like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא, the Bible expert, sits before רבי ינאי and says that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא the Bible expert was sitting before רבי ינאי. He sat and said: the הלכה is like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story in which רבי חנינא states the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. This sets up רבי ינאי's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far, the רבי יהודה ruling has come from עולא and רבי יצחק נפחא (step 24). Here רבי חנינא says the same thing, but this time in front of his teacher רבי ינאי.

keyTerms.meaning: A Bible expert, someone who knows the פסוקים well
Before him / in front of him

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina the Bible expert was sitting
phrases.notes: קָרָא here is a title for him: someone who knows the פסוקים well.

phrases.english: before Rabbi Yannai,
and he was sitting and saying:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְתֵיב רַבִּי חֲנִינָא קָרָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the question of the final הלכה raised in step 24
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי חנינא, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה: if the father is alive, the estate goes to the father

steps.title: רבי ינאי rejects the ruling: the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי sharply tells רבי חנינא to go outside and recite his פסוקים there. The הלכה is not like רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go out and read your פסוקים outside. The הלכה is not like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי strongly rejects רבי חנינא's ruling and says the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His words are a sharp put-down. He is telling רבי חנינא to stick to his פסוקים and leave deciding הלכה to others. This is a strong opinion against the ruling of עולא and רבי יצחק נפחא in step 24.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the rulings. עולא and רבי יצחק נפחא (step 24) and רבי חנינא say the הלכה is like רבי יהודה, but רבי ינאי says it is not.
steps.whatToRemember: On whether the יבם inherits while the father is alive, there is a real dispute about the הלכה. רבי ינאי firmly holds that the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: פּוֹק קְרִי קְרָיָיךְ לְבָרָא,
phrases.english: He said to him: Go out and read your verses outside,
phrases.notes: A sharp rebuke. He is saying, go recite your פסוקים outside, because ruling on הלכה is not your area.

phrases.english: the halakha is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: פּוֹק קְרִי קְרָיָיךְ לְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי חנינא's ruling from step 30
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי ינאי holds that this is simply not the הלכה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי ינאי, the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה

steps.title: A תנא recites that the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites in front of רב נחמן that the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רב נחמן: The הלכה is not like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second story, much like the one with רבי חנינא and רבי ינאי. A reciter of ברייתות states that the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה, and this sets up רב נחמן's reaction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling fits what רבי ינאי said in step 31. The new question the גמרא will raise is not whether the ruling is right. It is why anyone needs to say it out loud at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A person whose job in the study hall was to memorize and recite ברייתות

phrases.english: A tanna recited before Rav Nachman:
phrases.notes: Here a תנא is not one of the Sages of the משנה. He is someone who memorized ברייתות and recited them for the Sages.

phrases.english: The halacha is not like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story whose ruling matches רבי ינאי's rejection of רבי יהודה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה is not like רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious? We always follow the majority
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks why the ruling is needed, since the הלכה always follows the many against one Sage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: So whom is the הלכה like? Like the רבנן? That is obvious! When one Sage argues with many, the הלכה follows the many!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges the ruling the תנא just recited. Saying 'not like רבי יהודה' only means 'like the רבנן', and everyone already knows that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה is a single Sage, and the רבנן are the majority. The basic rule is that when one argues against many, we follow the many. So the line in the ברייתא looks like it adds nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why say it?
The Sages, meaning the majority opinion

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying the ruling is wrong. He agrees with it. He is only asking why it needs to be said.

phrases.english: He said to him: But then like whom?
Like the Rabbis?
That is obvious! One against many,
the halacha is like the many!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אֶלָּא כְּמַאן כְּרַבָּנַן פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ruling recited in step 32
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's line 'the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general rule already decides for the majority over a single Sage, so the line seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Should I remove the line?
steps.stepSummary: The תנא asks רב נחמן whether he should erase the ruling from his recitation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא said to him: Should I remove it?
steps.whatsHappening: The תנא reacts to רב נחמן's challenge. If the line adds nothing, maybe he should stop reciting it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא assumes that a line which teaches nothing new should not be part of the ברייתא. This question sets up רב נחמן's answer about where the line came from.

keyTerms.meaning: Should I remove it (take it out of the text)?

phrases.english: He said to him: Should I remove it?!
phrases.notes: Here the תנא is the one speaking. He offers to drop the line from his recitation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The תנא responds to the challenge of 'it's obvious' by offering to delete the line
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the unnecessary line should be taken out of the ברייתא

steps.title: Keep it: you were taught the opposite and fixed it correctly
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says not to remove it. The תנא was taught 'the הלכה is like רבי יהודה', found it hard, and flipped it, and he flipped it correctly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. You were taught 'the הלכה is like רבי יהודה', it was hard for you, and you reversed it. And the way you reversed it, you reversed it well.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains how the strange line got into the ברייתא and tells the תנא to keep it. The line is correct, even though it sounds obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Originally the ברייתא said the הלכה is like רבי יהודה. That sounded wrong to the תנא because it goes against the majority, so he changed it to 'not like רבי יהודה'. רב נחמן approves the change, which agrees with רבי ינאי's ruling in step 31.
steps.whatToRemember: The final ruling stands: the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה. Both רבי ינאי and רב נחמן agree, and the line stays in the ברייתא because it was a correct fix of an earlier version.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows why a ברייתא may say something that looks obvious. The line can be left over from a correction of an earlier version that taught the opposite.

phrases.english: He said to him: No.
You — they taught you 'the halacha [is like Rabbi Yehuda],'
and it was difficult for you,
and you reversed it.
And as for the way you reversed it,
you reversed it well.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לָא אַתְּ הֲלָכָה אַתְנְיֻיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תנא's question from step 34 and resolves the challenge from step 33
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Do not remove it. The line comes from a correct reversal of an earlier version that ruled like רבי יהודה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is not like רבי יהודה, and the ברייתא's line saying so is correct.

steps.title: New משנה: after חליצה, each is forbidden to the other's relatives
steps.stepSummary: A man who does חליצה with his יבמה becomes forbidden to her relatives, and she becomes forbidden to his relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who does חליצה with his יבמה is forbidden to her relatives, and she is forbidden to his relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. It teaches that חליצה creates a family connection that forbids certain relatives on both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though חליצה ends the bond without marriage, the man and the woman are still treated as connected. So close relatives of each side become off-limits to the other, as if he had married and then divorced her.

keyTerms.meaning: One who performs חליצה, the ceremony that releases the יבמה

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who performs chalitza with his yevama —
he is forbidden to her relatives,
and she is forbidden to his relatives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After חליצה, he is forbidden to her relatives and she is forbidden to his relatives.
